source.text: Τότε ἤρξατο ὀνειδίζειν τὰς πόλεις ἐν αἷς ἐγένοντο αἱ πλεῖσται δυνάμεις αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐ μετενόησαν·

records.literal_gloss: Then he began to reproach the cities in which happened the most miracles of him, because not they repented:

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to reproach the towns in which most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty works had happened, because they did not repent:
en.B: Then Jesus began to reproach the towns that had seen most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty works, for they had not repented.
en.R: Then Jesus began to speak strongly against the towns where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done most of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} miracles. The people there had not turned away from their sins and come back to God.

es.L: Entonces comenzó a reprochar a las ciudades en que habían ocurrido la mayor parte de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} obras poderosas, porque no se arrepintieron:
es.B: Entonces Jesús comenzó a reprender a las ciudades que habían visto la mayor parte de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} obras poderosas, porque no se habían arrepentido.
es.R: Después Jesús comenzó a hablar con dureza contra los pueblos donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había hecho la mayoría de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} milagros. La gente de allí no había dejado sus pecados para volver a Dios.

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à faire des reproches aux villes où avaient eu lieu la plupart de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} actes de puissance, parce qu’elles ne s’étaient pas repenties :
fr.B: Alors Jésus se mit à adresser des reproches aux villes qui avaient vu la plupart de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} miracles, car elles ne s’étaient pas repenties.
fr.R: Alors Jésus a commencé à parler durement contre les villes où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait la plupart de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} miracles. Les gens de ces villes ne s’étaient pas détournés de leurs péchés pour revenir à Dieu.

sw.L: Kisha akaanza kuikemea miji ambamo matendo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mengi ya nguvu yalifanyika, kwa sababu haikutubu:
sw.B: Kisha Yesu alianza kuilaumu miji iliyokuwa imeona matendo {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mengi ya nguvu, kwa kuwa haikutubu.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alianza kuisema vikali miji ambamo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alifanya miujiza {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mingi. Watu wa huko hawakuacha dhambi zao na kumrudia Mungu.

vi.L: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu quở trách các thành đã chứng kiến phần lớn các việc quyền năng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì họ đã không ăn năn:
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu quở trách các thành đã thấy phần lớn các việc quyền năng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì dân các thành ấy đã không ăn năn.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu bắt đầu nói những lời nghiêm khắc về các thành mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm nhiều phép lạ nhất. Dân ở đó đã không chịu từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그때 그분이 자기의 능력 있는 일들이 가장 많이 일어난 도시들을 꾸짖기 시작하셨다. 그들이 회개하지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그때 예수께서는 자기가 능력 있는 일을 가장 많이 행하신 도시들을 꾸짖기 시작하셨다. 그 도시들이 회개하지 않았기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그때 예수께서는 기적을 가장 많이 행하신 도시들을 엄하게 꾸짖기 시작하셨다. 그곳 사람들이 죄에서 돌이켜 하나님께 돌아오지 않았기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: mighty works: acts of power, miracles
decisions.reason: The plural of the word for power means deeds that show God's power.

decisions.choice: repent: turn from sin back to God
decisions.reason: See the notes on 3:2 and 4:17. The miracles called for a changed life.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("comenzó"), where there is nothing to capitalise, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: arrepentirse (L, B); dejar sus pecados para volver a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for turning from sin back to God (meaning decision m2); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal; speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading, while Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: actes de puissance (L), miracles (B, R); se repentir (L, B), se détourner de ses péchés pour revenir à Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the sense of the word, "acts of power" (m1), as in Luke 10:13; Balanced and Readable say "miracles". "Se repentir" is the term sheet's word; Readable spells it out as the English does (m2). The same for 11:21 and 11:23.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}; no span on the verbs
decisions.reason: The English "he" and "his" take the setting. Swahili carries the subject in the verb prefix (akaanza), which cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives take the span, as in John. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: kutubu (L, B); kuacha dhambi na kumrudia Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for turning from sin back to God (meaning decision m2); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "việc quyền năng" (L, B); "phép lạ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 9:39 and Matthew 7:22: acts of power (meaning decision). Also in 11:21 and 11:23.

decisions.choice: "ăn năn" (L, B); "từ bỏ tội lỗi và quay về với Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:2 and Mark 1:4: turning from sin back to God (meaning decision). Also in 11:21.

decisions.choice: "능력 있는 일" (L, B), "기적" (R); "회개하다" (L, B), "죄에서 돌이켜 하나님께 돌아오다" (R), through 11:20-24
decisions.reason: Mighty works are acts of power (meaning decision); "능력" is the Korean Mark's word for the power that went out from Jesus (5:30). "회개하다" and its Readable explanation as settled in the Korean Mark 1:4 and 1:15.

source.text: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγένοντο αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ μετενόησαν.

records.literal_gloss: Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; for if in Tyre and Sidon had happened the miracles having happened in you, long ago then in sackcloth and ashes they would have repented.

en.L: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if in Tyre and Sidon had happened the mighty works that happened in you, long ago they would have repented in sackcloth and ashes.
en.B: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Had Tyre and Sidon seen the mighty works done among you, they would have turned from their sins long ago, dressed in sackcloth and sitting in ashes.
en.R: "How terrible it will be for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! I did many miracles in your towns. If I had done them in Tyre and Sidon, the people there would have turned from their sins long ago. They would have put on rough clothes and sat in ashes to show how sorry they were.

es.L: «¡Ay de ti, Corazín! ¡Ay de ti, Betsaida! Porque si en Tiro y en Sidón se hubieran hecho las obras poderosas que se hicieron en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, hace tiempo que se habrían arrepentido en saco y ceniza.
es.B: «¡Ay de ti, Corazín! ¡Ay de ti, Betsaida! Si Tiro y Sidón hubieran visto las obras poderosas que se hicieron entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, hace mucho tiempo que se habrían arrepentido, vestidas de saco y sentadas en ceniza.
es.R: «¡Qué terrible será para ti, Corazín! ¡Qué terrible para ti, Betsaida! Hice muchos milagros en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pueblos. Si los hubiera hecho en Tiro y en Sidón, la gente de allí hace mucho que habría dejado sus pecados. Se habrían puesto ropa áspera y se habrían sentado en ceniza para mostrar que lo lamentaban.

fr.L: « Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Car si à Tyr et à Sidon avaient eu lieu les actes de puissance qui ont eu lieu chez vous, il y a longtemps qu’elles se seraient repenties dans le sac et la cendre.
fr.B: « Malheur à toi, Chorazin ! Malheur à toi, Bethsaïda ! Si Tyr et Sidon avaient vu les miracles accomplis chez vous, il y a longtemps que leurs habitants se seraient repentis, vêtus de sacs et assis dans la cendre.
fr.R: « Quel malheur pour toi, Chorazin ! Quel malheur pour toi, Bethsaïda ! J’ai fait beaucoup de miracles dans vos villes. Si je les avais faits à Tyr et à Sidon, les gens de là-bas se seraient détournés de leurs péchés depuis longtemps. Ils auraient mis des habits de toile grossière et ils se seraient assis dans la cendre pour montrer leur regret.

sw.L: "Ole wako, Korazini! Ole wako, Bethsaida! Kwa maana kama katika Tiro na Sidoni yangalifanyika matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwenu, zamani sana wangekuwa wametubu wakiwa katika magunia na majivu.
sw.B: "Ole wako, Korazini! Ole wako, Bethsaida! Kama Tiro na Sidoni zingeliona matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwenu, zingekuwa zimetubu tangu zamani, watu wake wakivaa magunia na kuketi katika majivu.
sw.R: "Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako, Korazini! Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako, Bethsaida! Nilifanya miujiza mingi katika miji yenu. Kama ningeifanya katika Tiro na Sidoni, watu wa huko wangeacha dhambi zao zamani. Wangevaa nguo za magunia na kukaa katika majivu ili kuonyesha jinsi walivyojuta.

vi.L: "Khốn cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Khốn cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Vì nếu các việc quyền năng đã làm giữa các ngươi được làm tại Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, thì họ đã mặc áo vải gai, ngồi trong tro mà ăn năn từ lâu rồi.
vi.B: "Khốn cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Khốn cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Nếu Ty-rơ và Si-đôn được thấy những việc quyền năng đã làm giữa các ngươi, thì dân ở đó đã mặc áo vải gai, ngồi trong tro để tỏ lòng ăn năn từ lâu rồi.
vi.R: "Thật khốn khổ cho ngươi, Cô-ra-xin! Thật khốn khổ cho ngươi, Bết-sai-đa! Ta đã làm nhiều phép lạ trong các thành của các ngươi. Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm những phép lạ ấy ở Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, thì dân ở đó đã từ bỏ tội lỗi từ lâu rồi. Họ đã mặc áo vải thô và ngồi trong tro để tỏ ra mình hối tiếc.

ko.L: "고라신아, 너에게 화가 있다! 벳새다야, 너에게 화가 있다! 너희에게서 일어난 능력 있는 일들이 두로와 시돈에서 일어났더라면, 그들은 벌써 오래전에 굵은 베옷을 입고 재를 뒤집어쓰고 회개하였을 것이다.
ko.B: "고라신아, 너는 얼마나 불행하냐! 벳새다야, 너는 얼마나 불행하냐! 너희 가운데서 행한 능력 있는 일들을 두로와 시돈에서 행했더라면, 그곳 사람들은 벌써 오래전에 굵은 베옷을 입고 재 위에 앉아 회개하였을 것이다.
ko.R: "고라신아, 너에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 벳새다야, 너에게도 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 나는 너희 마을에서 기적을 많이 행했다. 내가 그 기적들을 두로와 시돈에서 행했더라면, 그곳 사람들은 벌써 오래전에 죄에서 돌이켰을 것이다. 그들은 거친 옷을 입고 재 위에 앉아서 자기들의 죄를 슬퍼했을 것이다.

decisions.choice: Chorazin and Bethsaida: Jewish towns near Capernaum at the north end of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Matthew records none of the miracles done there, but Jesus says they were many.

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast, condemned by the prophets
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke against them for their pride (Isaiah 23; Ezekiel 26-28). Jesus says they would have done better than the towns of Galilee.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and ashes: signs of grief and repentance
decisions.reason: People wore rough goat-hair cloth and sat in ashes to show sorrow for sin (Jonah 3:6; Daniel 9:3).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning
decisions.reason: The prophets used the word to lament those facing God's judgment (Isaiah 5:8-22).

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you (R); Woe to you (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the old word "woe".

decisions.choice: ¡Ay de ti! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible será para ti! (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m4); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the two towns, and "ciudad" is feminine, so the Peninsular form is "vosotras". "Ti" for each town alone is singular and takes no span.

decisions.choice: Malheur à toi (L, B); Quel malheur pour toi (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Luke 10:13: "Malheur à" is still understood in French, unlike English "woe"; Readable makes it an exclamation of grief and warning (m4).

decisions.choice: Ole wako (L, B); Itakuwa vibaya sana kwako (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this cry of grief and warning (meaning decision m4); Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "ngươi", "các ngươi" for the towns
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the towns themselves, as the prophets spoke to cities in their oracles of woe; "ngươi" is the form Vietnamese uses for that address. It keeps them apart from the crowds he is speaking to, who are "các người" (11:22, 11:24).

decisions.choice: "Cô-ra-xin", "Bết-sai-đa", "Ty-rơ", "Si-đôn"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations, as for Tyre and Sidon in Mark 7:24-31 and Bethsaida in John.

decisions.choice: "mặc áo vải gai, ngồi trong tro" (L, B); "áo vải thô" (R)
decisions.reason: Sackcloth and ashes were signs of grief and repentance (meaning decision); Vietnamese says what was done with them.

decisions.choice: "화가 있다" (L); "얼마나 불행하냐" (B); "끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다" (R) for ouai
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 13:17 and 14:21: Literal keeps the traditional "화가 있다" in a modern ending; here woe is a cry of grief and warning (meaning decision), which Balanced says with "불행하다" and Readable as a warning, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "고라신", "벳새다", "두로", "시돈"; "굵은 베옷" and "재" (L, B), "거친 옷" (R)
decisions.reason: Protestant name forms (docs/korean-style.md section 5; the Korean Mark 3:8). Sackcloth and ashes were signs of grief and repentance (meaning decision); Readable says what they showed.

source.text: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But I say to you, for Tyre and Sidon more tolerable will it be in day of judgment than for you.

en.L: But I tell you, for Tyre and Sidon it will be more bearable on [the] day of judgment than for you.
en.B: But I tell you this: on the day of judgment Tyre and Sidon will be better off than you.
en.R: But I tell you, on the day God judges all people, it will be easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.

es.L: Sin embargo, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que para Tiro y Sidón será más tolerable en [el] día de juicio que para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.
es.B: Pero esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: en el día del juicio, Tiro y Sidón saldrán mejor libradas que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el día en que Dios juzgue a todos, será más fácil para Tiro y Sidón que para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.

fr.L: Cependant, je vous le dis, pour Tyr et Sidon ce sera plus supportable au jour du jugement que pour vous.
fr.B: Mais je vous le dis : au jour du jugement, Tyr et Sidon s’en tireront mieux que vous.
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis : le jour où Dieu jugera tout le monde, cela ira moins mal pour Tyr et Sidon que pour vous.

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia, kwa Tiro na Sidoni itavumilika zaidi katika siku ya hukumu kuliko kwenu.
sw.B: Lakini nawaambieni hili: siku ya hukumu Tiro na Sidoni zitakuwa na hali nafuu kuliko ninyi.
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, siku ambayo Mungu atawahukumu watu wote, itakuwa afadhali kwa Tiro na Sidoni kuliko kwenu.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, đến ngày phán xét, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ được chịu nhẹ hơn các ngươi.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói cho các người biết: trong ngày phán xét, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ còn chịu nhẹ hơn các ngươi.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, vào ngày Đức Chúa Trời phán xét mọi người, Ty-rơ và Si-đôn sẽ bị phạt nhẹ hơn các ngươi.

ko.L: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 심판 날에는 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 더 견디기 쉬울 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 심판 날에는 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 오히려 나을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 하나님께서 모든 사람을 심판하시는 날에, 두로와 시돈이 너희보다 벌을 덜 받을 것이다.

decisions.choice: more bearable on the day of judgment: judgment will match what each place was given
alternatives: all who reject God are judged alike
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same of Sodom and Gomorrah in 10:15. Those who saw his works and still refused are more to blame than those who never saw them.

decisions.choice: but: more than that, I tell you
decisions.reason: The word adds a stronger statement.

decisions.choice: the day God judges all people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose judgment is meant.

decisions.choice: "các người" for "I tell you"; "các ngươi" for the towns
decisions.reason: The Greek has "you" (plural) for both; the first are the hearers, the second the towns addressed in 11:21, so Vietnamese keeps the forms apart.

decisions.choice: worded as the Korean Matthew 10:15 at each level
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same comparison as in 10:15 (meaning decision), so the Korean repeats it.

source.text: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ;

records.literal_gloss: And you, Capernaum, not to heaven will you be lifted up?

en.L: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven?
en.B: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted as high as heaven?
en.R: And you, Capernaum! Do you think you will be lifted up to heaven?

es.L: Y tú, Cafarnaúm, ¿acaso serás elevada hasta [el] cielo?
es.B: Y tú, Cafarnaúm, ¿serás exaltada hasta el cielo?
es.R: ¡Y tú, Cafarnaúm! ¿Crees que serás levantada hasta el cielo?

fr.L: Et toi, Capharnaüm, seras-tu élevée jusqu’au ciel ?
fr.B: Et toi, Capharnaüm, seras-tu élevée aussi haut que le ciel ?
fr.R: Et toi, Capharnaüm ! Penses-tu que tu seras élevée jusqu’au ciel ?

sw.L: Na wewe, Kapernaumu, je, utainuliwa hadi mbinguni?
sw.B: Na wewe, Kapernaumu, je, utatukuzwa juu hadi mbinguni?
sw.R: Nawe Kapernaumu! Je, unadhani utainuliwa mpaka mbinguni?

vi.L: Còn ngươi, Ca-bê-na-um, ngươi sẽ được nâng lên đến tận trời sao?
vi.B: Còn ngươi, Ca-bê-na-um, ngươi tưởng sẽ được tôn cao đến tận trời sao?
vi.R: Còn ngươi, Ca-bê-na-um! Ngươi nghĩ mình sẽ được nâng lên đến tận trời sao?

ko.L: 그리고 너 가버나움아, 네가 하늘까지 높아지겠느냐?
ko.B: 그리고 너 가버나움아, 네가 하늘까지 높아질 것 같으냐?
ko.R: 그리고 가버나움아! 너는 네가 하늘까지 높아질 것이라고 생각하느냐?

decisions.choice: lifted to heaven, brought down to Hades: Isaiah 14:13-15
decisions.reason: Isaiah mocks the king of Babylon, who said, "I will ascend to heaven," but is brought down to the place of the dead. Capernaum's honor of having Jesus live there (4:13) will not save it.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The negative at the start shows the answer, which the next sentence gives.

decisions.choice: will you be lifted up to heaven?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you who have been lifted up to heaven, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts make this a statement about Capernaum's present honor. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no: "높아지겠느냐" (L), "높아질 것 같으냐" (B), "생각하느냐" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects "no" (meaning decision); Korean shows that with the doubtful "-겠느냐" and "-ㄹ 것 같으냐".

source.text: ἕως ᾅδου καταβήσῃ· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Σοδόμοις ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν σοί, ἔμεινεν ἂν μέχρι τῆς σήμερον.

records.literal_gloss: To Hades you will go down; for if in Sodom had happened the miracles having happened in you, it would have remained until the today.

en.L: You will go down to Hades. For if in Sodom had happened the mighty works that happened in you, it would have remained until today.
en.B: No, you will go down to the realm of the dead. If Sodom had seen the mighty works done in you, it would still be standing today.
en.R: No, you will go down to the place of the dead. If I had done in Sodom the miracles I did in you, Sodom would still be here today.

es.L: Hasta [el] Hades bajarás; porque si en Sodoma se hubieran hecho las obras poderosas que se hicieron en ti, habría permanecido hasta hoy.
es.B: No, bajarás hasta el Hades. Si Sodoma hubiera visto las obras poderosas que se hicieron en ti, todavía seguiría en pie hoy.
es.R: No, bajarás al lugar de los muertos. Si yo hubiera hecho en Sodoma los milagros que hice en ti, Sodoma todavía existiría hoy.

fr.L: Jusqu’à l’Hadès tu descendras. Car si à Sodome avaient eu lieu les actes de puissance qui ont eu lieu chez toi, elle serait restée jusqu’à aujourd’hui.
fr.B: Non, tu descendras jusqu’au séjour des morts. Si Sodome avait vu les miracles accomplis chez toi, elle existerait encore aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Non, tu descendras jusqu’au séjour des morts. Si j’avais fait à Sodome les miracles que j’ai faits chez toi, Sodome serait encore là aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Hadi Kuzimu utashuka. Kwa maana kama katika Sodoma yangalifanyika matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwako, ingalibaki hadi leo.
sw.B: Hapana, utashuka mpaka Kuzimu. Kama Sodoma ingeliona matendo ya nguvu yaliyofanyika kwako, ingekuwa bado imesimama hadi leo.
sw.R: Hapana, utashuka mpaka Kuzimu, mahali pa wafu. Kama ningefanya katika Sodoma miujiza niliyofanya kwako, Sodoma ingekuwepo hadi leo.

vi.L: Ngươi sẽ xuống tận Ha-đét. Vì nếu các việc quyền năng đã làm giữa ngươi được làm tại Sô-đôm, thì thành ấy đã còn lại cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Không, ngươi sẽ bị đày xuống âm phủ. Nếu Sô-đôm được thấy những việc quyền năng đã làm giữa ngươi, thì thành ấy vẫn còn đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Không đâu, ngươi sẽ phải xuống nơi của người chết. Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm ở Sô-đôm những phép lạ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm nơi ngươi, thì Sô-đôm vẫn còn đến ngày nay.

ko.L: 너는 하데스까지 내려갈 것이다. 너에게서 일어난 능력 있는 일들이 소돔에서 일어났더라면, 그 도시가 오늘까지 남아 있었을 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 아니다. 너는 죽은 사람들의 세계로 떨어질 것이다. 너에게서 행한 능력 있는 일들을 소돔에서 행했더라면, 그 도시는 오늘까지 남아 있었을 것이다.
ko.R: 아니다. 너는 죽은 사람들이 가는 곳으로 떨어질 것이다. 내가 너에게서 행한 기적들을 소돔에서 행했더라면, 소돔은 오늘까지도 남아 있었을 것이다.

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead, the lowest place, opposite heaven
alternatives: hell, the place of final punishment
decisions.reason: Hades is the Greek name used for Sheol, the world of the dead. Here it stands for the deepest humiliation, as in Isaiah 14:15. It is a different word from Gehenna (5:22).

decisions.choice: Sodom: the city God destroyed for its wickedness
decisions.reason: See Genesis 19. Sodom was the byword for a city ripe for judgment (10:15).

decisions.choice: you will go down, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: you will be brought down, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have a passive verb, as in Isaiah 14:15. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the realm of the dead (B); the place of the dead (R); Hades (L)
decisions.reason: "Hades" is a Greek name that many readers do not know, and "hell" would confuse it with Gehenna. Balanced and Readable say what it is.

decisions.choice: No
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable answer the question of 11:23a.

decisions.choice: el Hades (L, B); el lugar de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Balanced keeps the name, as Literal does, where the English Balanced says "the realm of the dead"; Readable says what it is (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: l’Hadès (L); le séjour des morts (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as in Luke 10:15. "Le séjour des morts" is the established French phrase for the place of the dead; "l’enfer" would confuse it with Gehenna.

decisions.choice: Kuzimu, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the place of the dead, the lowest place, opposite heaven (meaning decision m1). Readable adds "mahali pa wafu" to say what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Ha-đét" (L); "âm phủ" (B); "nơi của người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: Hades is the place of the dead, the lowest place, opposite heaven (meaning decision), not the place of punishment (Gehenna, "địa ngục" in 10:28). Literal keeps the name, as the English Literal does; "âm phủ" is the usual word for the realm of the dead.

decisions.choice: "하데스" (L); "죽은 사람들의 세계" (B); "죽은 사람들이 가는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: Hades is the place of the dead, the lowest place, set against heaven (meaning decision, footnoted). "음부" is the older church word and no longer understood; "지옥" is kept for Gehenna (10:28). Literal keeps the name, as the English does.

source.text: πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι γῇ Σοδόμων ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ σοί.

records.literal_gloss: But I say to you that for land of Sodom more tolerable will it be in day of judgment than for you.

en.L: But I tell you that for [the] land of Sodom it will be more bearable on [the] day of judgment than for you."
en.B: But I tell you this: on the day of judgment the land of Sodom will be better off than you."
en.R: But I tell you, on the day God judges all people, it will be easier for the land of Sodom than for you."

es.L: Sin embargo, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que para [la] tierra de Sodoma será más tolerable en [el] día de juicio que para ti».
es.B: Pero esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: en el día del juicio, la tierra de Sodoma saldrá mejor librada que tú».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el día en que Dios juzgue a todos, será más fácil para la tierra de Sodoma que para ti».

fr.L: Cependant, je vous dis que pour la terre de Sodome ce sera plus supportable au jour du jugement que pour toi. »
fr.B: Mais je vous le dis : au jour du jugement, le pays de Sodome s’en tirera mieux que toi. »
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis : le jour où Dieu jugera tout le monde, cela ira moins mal pour le pays de Sodome que pour toi. »

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwamba kwa nchi ya Sodoma itavumilika zaidi katika siku ya hukumu kuliko kwako."
sw.B: Lakini nawaambieni hili: siku ya hukumu nchi ya Sodoma itakuwa na hali nafuu kuliko wewe."
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, siku ambayo Mungu atawahukumu watu wote, itakuwa afadhali kwa nchi ya Sodoma kuliko kwako."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người rằng, đến ngày phán xét, xứ Sô-đôm sẽ được chịu nhẹ hơn ngươi."
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói cho các người biết: trong ngày phán xét, xứ Sô-đôm sẽ còn chịu nhẹ hơn ngươi."
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người, vào ngày Đức Chúa Trời phán xét mọi người, xứ Sô-đôm sẽ bị phạt nhẹ hơn ngươi."

ko.L: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 심판 날에는 소돔 땅이 너보다 더 견디기 쉬울 것이다."
ko.B: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 심판 날에는 소돔 땅이 너보다 오히려 나을 것이다."
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 하나님께서 모든 사람을 심판하시는 날에, 소돔 땅이 너보다 벌을 덜 받을 것이다."

decisions.choice: more bearable on the day of judgment: judgment will match what each place was given
alternatives: all who reject God are judged alike
decisions.reason: Jesus says the same of Sodom and Gomorrah in 10:15. Those who saw his works and still refused are more to blame than those who never saw them.

decisions.choice: I tell you (plural) ... than for you (singular)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to his hearers about Capernaum, then turns back to address the town itself.

decisions.choice: the land of Sodom: Sodom and the towns of its plain
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:25 tells of the overthrow of the cities and the whole plain.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:les|os}} digo ... que para ti
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to many, then to Capernaum alone (meaning decision m2). Spanish shows the change, plural "les" and singular "ti", which English "you" cannot.

decisions.choice: nawaambia ... kuliko kwako
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to many, then to Capernaum alone (meaning decision m2). Swahili shows the change, plural "-wa-" and singular "kwako", which English "you" cannot.

decisions.choice: "các người" ... "ngươi"
decisions.reason: The Greek itself moves from the hearers (plural) to Capernaum (singular) (meaning decision), and Vietnamese shows it with the two forms.

decisions.choice: "너희에게 말한다" and "너보다": plural, then singular
decisions.reason: Jesus says "I tell you" in the plural and then "than for you" in the singular, to Capernaum (meaning decision); Korean keeps "너희" and "너" as the Greek has them.

source.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἔκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις·

records.literal_gloss: At that the time answering the Jesus said, I praise you, Father, Lord of the heaven and the earth, that you hid these from wise and understanding and revealed them to infants;

en.L: At that time Jesus responded and said, "I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hid these things from [the] wise and understanding and revealed them to little children.
en.B: At that time Jesus said, "Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} praise, because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have kept these things hidden from the wise and the knowledgeable and have made them known to little children.
en.R: Then Jesus prayed, "Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! You have hidden these things from people who are wise and well educated. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown them to people who are like little children.

es.L: En aquel tiempo, tomando Jesús la palabra, dijo: «Te alabo, Padre, Señor del cielo y de la tierra, porque ocultaste estas cosas a [los] sabios y [a los] inteligentes, y las revelaste a [los] pequeñitos.
es.B: En aquel tiempo Jesús dijo: «Padre, Señor del cielo y de la tierra, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alabo, porque has mantenido estas cosas ocultas a los sabios y a los instruidos, y se las has dado a conocer a los pequeños.
es.R: Entonces Jesús oró: «Padre, Señor del cielo y de la tierra, ¡{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alabo! Tú has escondido estas cosas de la gente sabia y con estudios. Pero se las has mostrado a los que son como niños pequeños.

fr.L: En ce temps-là, Jésus, prenant la parole, dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue, Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as caché ces choses aux sages et aux intelligents et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as révélées aux petits enfants.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, Jésus dit : « Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue, parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as tenu ces choses cachées aux sages et aux gens instruits, et que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as fait connaître aux petits enfants.
fr.R: Alors Jésus a prié : « Père, Seigneur du ciel et de la terre, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue ! Tu as caché ces choses aux gens sages et très instruits. Mais {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les as montrées à ceux qui sont comme de petits enfants.

sw.L: Katika wakati ule Yesu, akijibu, alisema, "Ninakusifu, Baba, Bwana wa mbingu na dunia, kwa kuwa uliyasitiri mambo haya mbali na wenye hekima na wenye ufahamu, ukayadhihirisha kwa watoto wadogo.
sw.B: Wakati huo Yesu alisema, "Baba, Bwana wa mbingu na dunia, ninakusifu, kwa sababu mambo haya umeyaweka sirini kwa wenye hekima na wenye elimu, na umeyafanya yajulikane kwa watoto wadogo.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliomba, "Baba, Bwana wa mbingu na dunia, nakusifu! Umeyaficha mambo haya kwa watu wenye hekima na elimu kubwa. Lakini umewaonyesha watu walio kama watoto wadogo.

vi.L: Vào lúc ấy, Đức Giê-xu đáp lời và nói: "Lạy Cha, Chúa của trời và đất, Con ngợi khen Cha, vì Cha đã giấu những điều này khỏi những người khôn ngoan và hiểu biết, và đã bày tỏ chúng cho những con trẻ.
vi.B: Lúc ấy Đức Giê-xu nói: "Lạy Cha, là Chúa của trời và đất, Con ngợi khen Cha, vì Cha đã giấu những điều này khỏi người khôn ngoan và người thông sáng, mà bày tỏ cho những con trẻ.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu cầu nguyện: "Lạy Cha, là Chúa của trời và đất, Con ngợi khen Cha! Cha đã giấu những điều này khỏi những người khôn ngoan và có học thức. Nhưng Cha đã cho những người giống như trẻ nhỏ được biết.

ko.L: 그때에 예수께서 응답하여 말씀하셨다. "하늘과 땅의 주님이신 아버지, 제가 아버지를 찬양합니다. 아버지께서 이것들을 지혜로운 사람들과 똑똑한 사람들에게는 숨기시고, 어린아이들에게는 드러내셨기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그때에 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "하늘과 땅의 주님이신 아버지, 제가 아버지를 찬양합니다. 아버지께서는 이 일을 지혜롭고 학식 있는 사람들에게는 감추시고, 어린아이들에게는 알려 주셨습니다.
ko.R: 그때 예수께서 기도하셨다. "하늘과 땅의 주님이신 아버지, 아버지를 찬양합니다! 아버지께서는 지혜롭고 많이 배운 사람들에게는 이 일을 감추셨습니다. 그러나 어린아이 같은 사람들에게는 알려 주셨습니다.

decisions.choice: I praise you: I openly give you thanks and acknowledge what you have done
alternatives: I confess my sins to you
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare openly. Addressed to God it is praise and thanks.

decisions.choice: these things: who Jesus is and what his works mean
decisions.reason: The towns saw the works and did not understand (11:20-24); the disciples have begun to see.

decisions.choice: little children: the simple and unlearned, such as the disciples
decisions.reason: The word means infants and so people without learning or standing. Compare 18:3 and 21:16.

decisions.choice: answering: responding to the situation, not to a question
decisions.reason: The word often introduces speech without a question before it.

decisions.choice: Jesus prayed
decisions.reason: Readable says that Jesus is speaking to God. The pronouns "you" for the Father take the deity_pronoun setting, except at the start of a sentence.

decisions.choice: tomando la palabra
decisions.reason: Jesus is responding to what has happened, not to a question (meaning decision m4); "tomar la palabra" is to begin to speak in answer to a situation. "Te" at the start of the prayer is capitalised either way and takes no span.

decisions.choice: watoto wadogo
decisions.reason: The simple and unlearned, such as the disciples (meaning decision m3). "Watoto wachanga" are babies; "watoto wadogo" are little children, the English picture.

decisions.choice: "Con" for "I" and "Cha" for "you" in Jesus's prayer, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms for Jesus speaking to the Father (John 17): "Cha" and "Con" are nouns of address, always capitalised, so the English setting spans on "you" have no counterpart; the same in 11:26.

decisions.choice: "những con trẻ" (L, B); "những người giống như trẻ nhỏ" (R)
decisions.reason: The simple and unlearned, such as the disciples (meaning decision); Readable says it is a picture, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays in 합쇼체, calls himself "저" and says "아버지" for "you"; "하늘과 땅의 주님"
decisions.reason: As the Korean John 17: the style guide has Jesus speak to the Father in 합쇼체, and Korean addresses a superior by title rather than "당신". The Father is addressed as Lord with the honorific "주님".

decisions.choice: "찬양합니다"; "어린아이들" (L, B), "어린아이 같은 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is open praise and acknowledgment of what God has done (meaning decision), which "찬양하다" says. The little children are the simple and unlearned (meaning decision); Readable says they are like children, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου.

records.literal_gloss: Yes, the Father, for thus good pleasure it was before you.

en.L: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Yes, Father, it pleased {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to have it so.
en.R: Yes, Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did this because it was what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wanted.

es.L: Sí, Padre, porque así fue agradable delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}.
es.B: Sí, Padre, porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quisiste que así fuera.
es.R: Sí, Padre, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} hiciste esto porque era lo que querías.

fr.L: Oui, Père, car c’est ainsi que cela a été agréable devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: Oui, Père, c’est ce qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a semblé bon.
fr.R: Oui, Père, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’as fait parce que c’est ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voulais.

sw.L: Ndiyo, Baba, kwa kuwa ndivyo ilivyopendeza mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Ndiyo, Baba, ulifanya hivi kwa sababu ndivyo ulivyotaka.

vi.L: Vâng, lạy Cha, vì điều ấy đẹp ý Cha.
vi.B: Vâng, lạy Cha, vì Cha vui lòng muốn như vậy.
vi.R: Vâng, lạy Cha, Cha đã làm như thế vì đó là điều Cha muốn.

ko.L: 그렇습니다, 아버지, 이렇게 하시는 것이 아버지 앞에서 기뻐하시는 뜻이었습니다.
ko.B: 그렇습니다, 아버지, 이것이 아버지께서 기뻐하신 뜻이었습니다.
ko.R: 그렇습니다, 아버지. 아버지께서는 원하셔서 이렇게 하셨습니다.

decisions.choice: good pleasure: God's gracious choice
decisions.reason: The word is related to the verb in 3:17 ("in whom I am well pleased"). God chose freely to work this way.

decisions.choice: the Father: a form with the article, used as an address
decisions.reason: Greek of this period can use the form with the article to address someone.

decisions.choice: "기뻐하시는 뜻" (L, B); "원하셔서" (R)
decisions.reason: Good pleasure is God's gracious choice (meaning decision); "기뻐하시는 뜻" says both his will and his delight in it.

source.text: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιγινώσκει τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, οὐδὲ τὸν πατέρα τις ἐπιγινώσκει εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.

records.literal_gloss: All things to me were handed over by the Father of me, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor the Father anyone knows except the Son and to whom if wills the Son to reveal.

en.L: All things have been handed over to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and [anyone] to whom the Son wills to reveal [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
en.B: My Father has entrusted everything to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one fully knows the Son except the Father, and no one fully knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son decides to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known.
en.R: My Father has given everything to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one really knows the Son except the Father. And no one really knows the Father except the Son. The Son also shows the Father to the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

es.L: Todo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fue entregado por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre, y nadie conoce al Hijo excepto el Padre, y tampoco conoce nadie al Padre excepto el Hijo y [aquel] a quien el Hijo quiera [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] revelar.
es.B: Mi Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha confiado todo. Nadie conoce de verdad al Hijo, sino el Padre, y nadie conoce de verdad al Padre, sino el Hijo y aquellos a quienes el Hijo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} quiere dar a conocer.
es.R: Mi Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado todo. Nadie conoce realmente al Hijo, sino el Padre. Y nadie conoce realmente al Padre, sino el Hijo. El Hijo también muestra al Padre a las personas que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} escoge.

fr.L: Toutes choses {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont été remises par {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, et personne ne connaît le Fils, sinon le Père, et personne non plus ne connaît le Père, sinon le Fils et [celui] à qui le Fils veut [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] révéler.
fr.B: Mon Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a tout confié. Personne ne connaît pleinement le Fils, sinon le Père, et personne ne connaît pleinement le Père, sinon le Fils et ceux à qui le Fils décide de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire connaître.
fr.R: Mon Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a tout donné. Personne ne connaît vraiment le Fils, sauf le Père. Et personne ne connaît vraiment le Père, sauf le Fils. Le Fils fait aussi connaître le Père aux personnes qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} choisit.

sw.L: Mambo yote yamekabidhiwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} na Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na hakuna anayemjua Mwana isipokuwa Baba, wala hakuna anayemjua Baba isipokuwa Mwana, na [yeyote] ambaye Mwana amekusudia kumfunulia [{{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}].
sw.B: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} amenikabidhi kila kitu. Hakuna anayemjua Mwana kikamilifu isipokuwa Baba, na hakuna anayemjua Baba kikamilifu isipokuwa Mwana na wale ambao Mwana ameamua kuwafunulia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} amenipa kila kitu. Hakuna anayemjua Mwana kwa kweli isipokuwa Baba. Na hakuna anayemjua Baba kwa kweli isipokuwa Mwana. Mwana pia huwaonyesha Baba wale ambao {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huwachagua.

vi.L: Mọi sự đã được Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giao cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và không ai biết Con ngoại trừ Cha, cũng không ai biết Cha ngoại trừ Con và người nào mà Con muốn bày tỏ [Cha] cho.
vi.B: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giao phó mọi sự cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Không ai biết rõ Con, ngoại trừ Cha; cũng không ai biết rõ Cha, ngoại trừ Con và những người mà Con muốn bày tỏ Cha cho họ.
vi.R: Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giao mọi sự cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Không ai thật sự biết Con, chỉ có Cha biết. Cũng không ai thật sự biết Cha, chỉ có Con biết. Con cũng cho những người Con chọn được biết Cha.

ko.L: 내 아버지께서 모든 것을 나에게 넘겨주셨다. 그리고 아버지 외에는 아무도 아들을 알지 못하고, 아들과 아들이 [아버지를] 드러내 주기로 뜻한 사람 외에는 아무도 아버지를 알지 못한다.
ko.B: 내 아버지께서 모든 것을 나에게 맡겨 주셨다. 아버지 외에는 아무도 아들을 온전히 알지 못한다. 그리고 아들과, 아들이 아버지를 알려 주기로 한 사람들 외에는 아무도 아버지를 온전히 알지 못한다.
ko.R: 내 아버지께서 모든 것을 나에게 주셨다. 아버지 외에는 아무도 아들을 참으로 알지 못한다. 그리고 아들 외에는 아무도 아버지를 참으로 알지 못한다. 아들은 자기가 택한 사람들에게 아버지를 알려 준다.

decisions.choice: all things have been handed over: the Father has given the Son all authority, including the knowledge of God
alternatives: only the teaching passed on to him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of handing on what one holds. Compare 28:18, "all authority ... has been given to me."

decisions.choice: knows: knows fully and personally
decisions.reason: The verb has a strengthening prefix. The knowing is the close knowledge of a father and son.

decisions.choice: the Son: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of the Father
decisions.reason: God called Jesus "my Son" at his baptism (3:17). Only the Son can make the Father known, as John 1:18 also says.

decisions.choice: fully knows (B); really knows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the force of the verb.

decisions.choice: "Con" and "Cha" with capitals, and the nouns repeated where the English has "him" and "he"
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son of the Father (meaning decision). Vietnamese repeats the nouns, which are capitalised and take no setting, so the English pronoun spans have no counterpart here.

decisions.choice: Jesus turns to the hearers in 해라체; "아들" without honorific, "아버지께서" with it
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as the Son (meaning decision), and a Korean speaker does not honor himself, as in the Korean John 17:1 where "아들" stays plain; the Father keeps "께서". The prayer has ended, so the speech level goes back to 해라체 for his hearers.

decisions.choice: "넘겨주다" (L), "맡겨 주다" (B); "알다" (L), "온전히 알다" (B), "참으로 알다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Father has given the Son all authority (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek verb, Balanced says "entrust". The verb for knowing means knowing fully and personally (meaning decision), which Balanced and Readable add.

source.text: Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι, κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Come to me all the toiling and having been burdened, and I will give rest you.

en.L: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest.
en.B: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who are worn out with work and weighed down with burdens, and I will give you rest.
en.R: Come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, all of you who are tired from hard work and from carrying heavy loads. I will give you rest.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, todos los agotados y sobrecargados, y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} daré reposo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, todos los que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} rendidos por el trabajo y aplastados por el peso de la carga, y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} daré alivio.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, todos los que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} cansados de trabajar duro y de llevar cargas pesadas. Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} daré descanso.

fr.L: Venez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous tous qui peinez et qui êtes chargés, et moi, je vous donnerai du repos.
fr.B: Venez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous tous qui êtes épuisés par le travail et accablés sous les fardeaux, et je vous donnerai le repos.
fr.R: Venez à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous tous qui êtes à bout de forces à cause du travail dur et des lourdes charges que vous portez. Je vous donnerai du repos.

sw.L: Njooni {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, ninyi nyote mnaochoka kwa taabu na mliotwikwa mizigo, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawapa pumziko.
sw.B: Njooni {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, nyote mliochoshwa na kazi ngumu na kuelemewa na mizigo mizito, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawapa pumziko.
sw.R: Njooni {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, nyote mliochoka kwa kufanya kazi ngumu na kubeba mizigo mizito. Nitawapa pumziko.

vi.L: Hãy đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, hỡi tất cả những ai lao khổ và gánh nặng, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho các con được nghỉ ngơi.
vi.B: Hỡi tất cả những ai làm lụng mệt nhọc và mang gánh nặng nề, hãy đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho các con được nghỉ ngơi.
vi.R: Hỡi tất cả những ai mệt mỏi vì làm việc vất vả và vì mang gánh nặng, hãy đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta sẽ cho các con được nghỉ ngơi.

ko.L: 수고하고 무거운 짐을 진 사람들은 모두 나에게로 오너라. 그러면 내가 너희를 쉬게 하겠다.
ko.B: 일에 지치고 무거운 짐에 짓눌린 사람들은 모두 나에게로 오너라. 내가 너희를 쉬게 하겠다.
ko.R: 힘든 일로 지치고 무거운 짐을 지고 있는 사람들은 모두 나에게 오너라. 내가 너희에게 쉼을 주겠다.

decisions.choice: toil: work until worn out
decisions.reason: The verb means to labor hard and grow weary.

decisions.choice: burdened: loaded down, including with the many rules laid on people by their teachers
decisions.reason: The same picture returns in 23:4, where the scribes and Pharisees tie heavy loads on people's shoulders. The invitation is open to all who are weighed down.

decisions.choice: come to me: wisdom's invitation
decisions.reason: In Sirach 51:23-27, a Jewish wisdom book written about two centuries earlier, the teacher calls the untaught to come, take wisdom's yoke on their necks, and find rest. Jesus speaks as wisdom herself (11:19).

decisions.choice: give rest: refresh, give relief
decisions.reason: The verb means to let someone stop and recover.

decisions.choice: los agotados y sobrecargados
decisions.reason: Two participles in the Greek: worn out with work (meaning decision m1) and loaded down (m2). Literal keeps them as two words, "sobrecargados" with the picture of a load that Balanced and Readable spell out.

decisions.choice: mliotwikwa mizigo
decisions.reason: Loaded down, as with a burden laid on one (meaning decision m2). "Kutwikwa" is to have a load put on one's head, the Greek picture.

decisions.choice: "các con" in 11:28-30
decisions.reason: An invitation to all who come to learn from him (11:29), so Jesus speaks with the warm "các con" of his teaching, not the "các người" of the rebuke in 11:7-24.

decisions.choice: "lao khổ và gánh nặng" (L); "làm lụng mệt nhọc và mang gánh nặng nề" (B)
decisions.reason: To toil is to work until worn out, and the burden includes the many rules laid on people (meaning decision); Vietnamese keeps both pictures.

decisions.choice: "수고하다" (L), "일에 지치다" (B), "힘든 일로 지치다" (R); "쉬게 하다" (L, B), "쉼을 주다" (R)
decisions.reason: To toil is to work until worn out, and the burden includes the many rules laid on people (meaning decision); the giving of rest is relief and refreshment (meaning decision). "안식" is kept for the Sabbath in 12:1-12, so the plain "쉬다" and "쉼" are used here.

source.text: ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς καὶ μάθετε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ, καὶ εὑρήσετε ἀνάπαυσιν ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Take the yoke of me upon you and learn from me, for gentle I am and humble in the heart, and you will find rest for the souls of you;

en.L: Take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke upon you and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
en.B: Put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke on your necks and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because I am gentle and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart is humble. Then you will find rest for your souls.
en.R: Take {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke and put it on, and learn from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am gentle and humble. And you will find rest for your souls.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} yugo y {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque soy manso y de corazón humilde, y {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} reposo para {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} almas;
es.B: {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} yugo sobre el cuello y {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque soy manso y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón es humilde. Así {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} reposo para {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alma.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} yugo y {{plural_you:pónganselo|ponéoslo}}, y {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Soy amable y humilde. Y {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}} descanso para {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} alma.

fr.L: Prenez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} joug sur vous et apprenez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, car je suis doux et humble de cœur, et vous trouverez du repos pour vos âmes.
fr.B: Placez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} joug sur votre cou et apprenez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, parce que je suis doux et que {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur est humble. Alors vous trouverez le repos pour vos âmes.
fr.R: Prenez {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} joug et mettez-le sur vous, et apprenez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Je suis doux et humble. Et vous trouverez le repos pour vos âmes.

sw.L: Chukueni nira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} juu yenu, mjifunze kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, kwa sababu ni mpole, mwenye moyo wa unyenyekevu, na mtapata pumziko kwa nafsi zenu;
sw.B: Vaeni nira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} shingoni mwenu, mjifunze kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, kwa kuwa ni mpole na moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni mnyenyekevu. Ndipo mtakapopata pumziko kwa nafsi zenu.
sw.R: Chukueni nira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} mjivike, na mjifunze kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}. Mimi ni mpole na mnyenyekevu. Nanyi mtapata pumziko kwa nafsi zenu.

vi.L: Hãy mang ách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên các con và học theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hiền lành và khiêm nhường trong lòng, thì các con sẽ tìm được sự nghỉ ngơi cho linh hồn mình.
vi.B: Hãy mang ách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lên vai và học theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hiền lành và có lòng khiêm nhường. Như vậy linh hồn các con sẽ được nghỉ ngơi.
vi.R: Hãy nhận lấy ách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà mang, và hãy học theo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta hiền lành và khiêm nhường. Rồi linh hồn các con sẽ được nghỉ ngơi.

ko.L: 너희 위에 내 멍에를 메고 나에게서 배워라. 나는 온유하고 마음이 겸손하기 때문이다. 그러면 너희가 너희 영혼을 위한 쉼을 얻을 것이다.
ko.B: 내 멍에를 너희 목에 메고 나에게서 배워라. 나는 온유하고 마음이 겸손하다. 그러면 너희는 영혼의 쉼을 얻을 것이다.
ko.R: 내 멍에를 메고 나에게서 배워라. 나는 온유하고 겸손하다. 그러면 너희 영혼이 쉼을 얻을 것이다.

decisions.choice: yoke: the wooden bar that joins working animals at the neck; a picture of teaching that one takes on
decisions.reason: A yoke let animals pull a load. Jewish teachers spoke of taking on the yoke of the law or of the kingdom, and Sirach 51:26 of wisdom's yoke. To take Jesus's yoke is to follow his teaching.

decisions.choice: you will find rest for your souls: Jeremiah 6:16
decisions.reason: God tells Israel to walk in the good, ancient way, and they will find rest for their souls. Israel refused; Jesus offers that rest.

decisions.choice: gentle and humble in heart: meek and lowly, not harsh or proud
decisions.reason: "Gentle" is the word of 5:5 and 21:5. "Humble" means lowly; Jesus is a teacher unlike those who load others down (23:4).

decisions.choice: learn from me: become my disciple
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for disciple, one who learns.

decisions.choice: on your necks
decisions.reason: Balanced shows where a yoke is worn.

decisions.choice: "ách" for the yoke; "lên vai" (B)
decisions.reason: The wooden bar that joins working animals at the neck, a picture of teaching one takes on (meaning decision). "gông" is a prisoner's collar and would change the picture. Balanced says "lên vai" where the English says "on your necks": a Vietnamese yoke rests on the shoulders.

decisions.choice: "hiền lành và khiêm nhường"
decisions.reason: Meek and lowly, not harsh or proud (meaning decision), in common modern words.

decisions.choice: "멍에"; "온유하다", "겸손하다"; "쉼"
decisions.reason: The yoke is the bar on a working animal's neck, a picture of teaching one takes on (meaning decision); Korean has the same word and picture, as in the Korean Mark 10:9. "온유" and "겸손" say meek and lowly, not harsh or proud (meaning decision). "쉼" repeats the rest of 11:28.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ ζυγός μου χρηστὸς καὶ τὸ φορτίον μου ἐλαφρόν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The for yoke of me kind and the burden of me light is.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke [is] easy, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burden is light."
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} yoke is easy to wear, and the load I give is light."
en.R: The yoke I give you is easy to wear. The load I ask you to carry is light."

es.L: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} yugo [es] bueno, y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} carga es ligera».
es.B: Porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} yugo se lleva con facilidad, y la carga que yo doy es ligera».
es.R: El yugo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} doy es fácil de llevar. La carga que {{plural_you:les|os}} pido que {{plural_you:lleven|llevéis}} es ligera».

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} joug [est] facile à porter, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fardeau est léger. »
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} joug est facile à porter, et la charge que je donne est légère. »
fr.R: Le joug que je vous donne est facile à porter. La charge que je vous demande de porter est légère. »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa nira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [ni] njema, na mzigo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ni mwepesi."
sw.B: Kwa maana nira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} haiumizi kuivaa, na mzigo ninaowapa ni mwepesi."
sw.R: Nira ninayowapa ni rahisi kuivaa. Mzigo ninaowaomba mbebe ni mwepesi."

vi.L: Vì ách của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} dễ chịu, và gánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nhẹ nhàng."
vi.B: Vì ách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mang cho các con thì dễ chịu, và gánh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giao cho các con thì nhẹ nhàng."
vi.R: Ách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho các con mang thì dễ chịu. Gánh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo các con mang thì nhẹ."

ko.L: 내 멍에는 편하고 내 짐은 가볍기 때문이다."
ko.B: 내 멍에는 메기 편하고, 내가 지우는 짐은 가볍다."
ko.R: 내가 주는 멍에는 메기 편하다. 내가 지라고 하는 짐은 가볍다."

decisions.choice: easy: kind, good, fitting well
decisions.reason: The word means good or kind. Of a yoke it means one that fits well and does not rub. Jesus still calls people to obey (5:19-20).

decisions.choice: burden: the load Jesus asks his followers to carry

decisions.choice: easy (L); easy to wear (B, R)
